analysis.title: Marex Group (MRX): Growth trends remain robust despite a more normalized trading environment; Reiterate Buy post mgmt meeting
key_insights: GS hosted a meeting with MRX CEO Ian Lowitt after 3Q26 results and reiterates Buy with greater conviction in earnings growth durability into 2027, even as trading volumes normalize after a strong 2026.

3Q adjusted PBT rose 6% q/q to a record $176mn. Management said October trends were around the average levels seen this year, citing market share gains, recent M&A and a more diversified revenue base.

Management is comfortable with 10%-20% adjusted PBT growth in 2027 despite tough 2026 comps. The outlook includes the full-year contribution from Levmet/Webb and Bright Point and no contribution from other prospective acquisitions.

Prime Services 3Q revenue was $115mn, roughly 2x y/y. Balances are still roughly 2x year-ago levels, with share gains offsetting lower balances tied to repriced AI-related stocks and levered ETFs. About half of Prime is related to levered ETFs.

Management does not expect Prime to repeat the roughly 100% growth seen this year, given the capital intensity of on-balance-sheet Prime, but still sees healthy growth. MRX won a meaningful client from a competitor in the past week.
Clearing average client balances were $18.7bn in 3Q vs $13.3bn a year ago, with new client onboarding adding more than $1bn of balances YTD.

Treasury cross-margining has six clients live and 15 in the pipeline, including several large hedge funds. Current run-rate revenue is around $15-$20mn, and management said it could approach ~$50mn, though competition may pressure pricing.
Management called 3Q a reasonable base for Market Making earnings. It described the business as relatively agency-like, with positions exited quickly and VaR only in the single-digit millions.

MRX is live as an FCM on Kalshi with six major institutional clients ready to trade and plans to add Polymarket. Management values the relationships with large hedge funds more than near-term prediction-market revenue.
MRX completed its first OTC swap on Canton Network and is working with exchanges on compute-related futures products.
Payments targets a launch around 4Q26/1Q27, focused on non-G7 currencies, building on the Hamilton Court platform. FX revenues are approaching 3x the pre-acquisition run rate.

3Q adjusted PBT margin was 23.7%, up ~300bps y/y, vs 21% in 2025. Management now sees a path to ~30% over time, up from its earlier mid-20s framework, with more gradual expansion after the 2026 step-up.

Four acquisitions have agreed terms, each roughly the size of Bright Point (~$25mn of PBT) and mostly in Clearing/Prime in Asia and Latin America, with 4-6 more further back in the pipeline. Most could be signed in 4Q26/1Q27, with meaningful earnings contribution unlikely before 2H27.

GS raised 2027/2028 EPS estimates to $7.66/$9.23 from $7.25/$8.80 on higher clearing NII, the latest forward curve and share gains with larger institutional clients. The 2026 estimate is largely unchanged at $5.94.
GS raised its 12-month price target to $88 from $84, based on ~10.5x Q5-Q8 P/E (unchanged). With the price at $67.91, implied upside is 29.6%.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy and raises the target to $88 from $84 on higher 2027/2028 EPS estimates. Drivers are clearing NII, the forward curve and institutional share gains.

tension_points.bull_case: GS sees a solid exit rate into 2027, with management comfortable with 10%-20% adjusted PBT growth, structural growth in Prime, Clearing and Market Making, margin expansion toward ~30%, and an M&A pipeline not included in guidance.
tension_points.bear_case: Trading volumes are normalizing after a strong 2026, 2026 comps are tough, and Prime is not expected to repeat ~100% growth. Prime balances face pressure from levered ETFs and repriced AI stocks, and Treasury cross-margining pricing may face competition.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Lower rates or lower volatility, which GS lists as downside risks, or integration problems with acquisitions such as Levmet/Webb and Bright Point.

theme_stances.key_argument: Structural growth in Prime, Clearing and Market Making, plus margin expansion and M&A, support earnings growth into 2027 despite normalizing volumes.
theme_stances.evidence: greater conviction in the durability of MRX's earnings growth into 2027
